purpose: Lenvatinib is used to treat certain types of cancer, including thyroid cancer, kidney cancer, and liver cancer. It may also be used in combination with another medicine called pembrolizumab for certain types of uterine cancer. Your doctor prescribed it because it helps slow or stop cancer from growing and spreading.
how_it_works: Lenvatinib works by blocking certain proteins in the body called kinases that cancer cells need to grow and form new blood vessels. Think of it like cutting off the supply lines that the tumor needs to survive and spread. By blocking these signals, the medicine helps starve the cancer and slow its growth.
common_side_effects: High blood pressure, tiredness, diarrhea, decreased appetite, weight loss, nausea, mouth sores, joint or muscle pain, swelling in the hands or feet, hoarse voice, stomach pain, and rash on the hands or feet (redness, pain, or peeling).
warnings: This medicine can cause serious high blood pressure, which needs to be checked regularly. It can cause heart problems, liver damage, kidney problems, or blood clots. It may cause a hole in the stomach or bowel (perforation), which is rare but serious. It is very harmful to an unborn baby, so do not get pregnant while taking it and use reliable birth control. Tell your doctor right away if you have severe headache, chest pain, trouble breathing, unusual bleeding, or severe stomach pain.
typical_dosing: The usual adult dose is 24 mg (two 10 mg capsules and one 4 mg capsule) taken by mouth once a day, with or without food, at the same time each day. For some cancers or in combination with other medicines, the dose may be different. Swallow the capsules whole or dissolve them in water or apple juice if needed. Your doctor may lower your dose if you have side effects.
